data.narrative:
Alif Semiconductor is a Series C-stage chip design company that has raised $186M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a peer universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-tech counterparts, with primary comparables including d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series C), Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), DEEPX ($529M, Series C), and Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $186M capital base, yielding $316M. Peer-median anchoring across the four sampled same-sector and same/adjacent-stage companies produces a $1.5B midpoint, with observed range of $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (21.0x median across the three public semiconductors) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $269M (floor) to $1.7B (ceiling), with a median estimate of $908M across the two applicable methods. The wide dispersion—reflecting heterogeneity in private chip valuations and stage-dependent comparables—underscores material uncertainty around market positioning and technical de-risking relative to the peer set. Revenue visibility and pathway to commercialization remain key valuation drivers not captured in this quantitative exercise.
